transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO - Apex), Jon (Lead Platform Eng), Sara (Security)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to talk through how Redwood would integrate with Apex's stack. quick round-robin?
[00:07] Maya: hey, Maya here, CTO, we'll be owning the decision and timeline.
[00:10] Jon: Jon, platform, i'll be hands-on for infra and gateways.
[00:13] Sara: Sara - security architect, i'll review compliance and network stuff.
[00:17] Alex: awesome, from Redwood, priya will cover technical integration and sample configs. priya?
[00:22] Priya: hi! quick agenda: SDKs, langchain/llamaindex adapters, our recommended gateway patterns, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks and then questions.
[00:33] Alex: also quick note - we support hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem installs. decision usually depends on latency/cost and compliance.
[00:42] Maya: right. compliance is a hard requirement for certain product lines - we may need VPC or even on-prem for payment flows.
[00:49] Sara: can you outline the difference in the integration surface between hosted and private? like what code changes, network routes, and tooling do we need?
[00:56] Priya: yes. hosted is the simplest: SDK calls to api.redwood.ai with mTLS or api keys, tenant-level RBAC and audit logs in the console. Dedicated is similar but you get reserved GPU pools and a private tenancy with IP allowlists. Private (VPC) gives you a control plane that talks over peered VPC and data plane in your network — so traffic doesn't traverse public internet.
[01:20] Jon: for private, is there a lightweight gateway you recommend? we run an Envoy-based edge and have a Kong cluster as well.
[01:28] Priya: we commonly front Redwood requests with a simple proxy pattern: Envoy or Kong handles auth + rate limiting and routes to the Redwood endpoint. we provide sample Envoy configs. if you want in-cluster, we can also run a sidecar shim that handles retries, backpressure, and key rotation.
[01:45] Jon: nice. does Redwood expose health/check endpoints so our gateway can circuit-break?
[01:49] Priya: yes, health, metrics (Prometheus), and readiness endpoints are available in Dedicated/Private. hosted exposes status pages and per-tenant telemetry via the console and we also stream metrics via a secure webhook or prometheus federation for customers on enterprise plans.
[02:04] Maya: we use LangChain heavily for orchestration. how smooth is the integration? any gotchas?
[02:09] Priya: we have first-class LangChain adapters and LlamaIndex connectors. the starter repo includes prompt templates, retry logic for streaming responses, and token accounting helpers. caveat: some low-level param names differ between langchain llm wrappers and our SDK so we include mapping helpers in the examples.
[02:29] Jon: tokens and cost accounting — can you emit per-request token counts via headers or in logs? we need to attribute cost per product line.
[02:35] Priya: yes, we provide per-request token breakdowns in both logs and the console. for hosted: you get token-level cost in the console and can pull via API. for dedicated/private, we surface the same metrics via Prometheus labels and a cost-exporter that maps to your billing metrics.
[02:53] Sara: regarding encryption and KMS — for private we want HSM-backed keys and no plaintext logs. supported?
[02:59] Priya: absolutely. Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, envelope encryption, and you can opt out of storing any request payloads. we also provide audit logs to your SIEM.
[03:10] Alex: are there any constraints around function calling / streaming with your best-performing models on smaller GPUs?
[03:15] Priya: streaming is supported across models; for some quantized variants on smaller GPUs, latency characteristics change. we include per-model performance profiles in the catalog so you can pick a model that balances latency vs cost. function-calling uses the same streaming channel but we recommend models with lower hallucination for structured outputs.
[03:36] Jon: gateway rate limiting — we want to enforce per-customer and per-route quotas. can quotas be expressed on your side or do we have to enforce entirely in our gateway?
[03:44] Priya: both. on gateway side you can enforce hard rate limits. Redwood supports soft quotas on the service-side with callbacks for quota-exhausted events; and for Dedicated/Private you can configure per-tenant quotas and throttling policies in the control plane.
[03:59] Maya: for the POC we want to simulate production traffic and ramp to 200 rps with spikes. is that doable on hosted sandbox?
[04:06] Alex: yes, we can provision a sandbox with increased limits for the POC. it'll be separate from prod and we'll provide traffic shaping guidance.
[04:13] Jon: observability hooks — do you integrate with our existing tracing? we run Jaeger and DataDog.
[04:18] Priya: we emit OpenTelemetry compatible traces and will forward spans to Jaeger or Datadog through a secure exporter. logs can be pushed to your S3 or to DataDog. We also provide token-level cost traces so you can pivot by request id.
[04:33] Sara: auditability for legal — do you provide immutable audit logs with retention controls?
[04:37] Priya: yes, retention is configurable. Private and Dedicated customers can set retention policies and export immutable logs to your log storage; we support append-only exports with signed timestamps if you need chain-of-custody.
[04:50] Ethan: product question — how intrusive is the SDK change if we swap from OpenAI to Redwood, since we already have a wrapper?
[04:56] Priya: we mimic a lot of OpenAI surface patterns in the SDK, and we have a drop-in adapter for many existing wrappers. plus the LangChain adapter reduces friction. usually it's a few lines to change endpoints and a small mapping layer for a few params.
[05:09] Jon: any rate limit headers on responses so we can do client-side throttling?
[05:12] Priya: yes for hosted we send X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and a retry-after when applicable. For Dedicated/Private, your policy enforcement lives in the control plane but we can also configure middleware to return compatible headers.
[05:27] Maya: regarding data residency — some EU customers must keep data in eu-west only. how granular is region pinning?
[05:33] Priya: you can pin model workloads to region at the project level; Private lets you deploy entirely within your VPC region. for hosted we also provide EU-only tenancy for enterprise customers.
[05:44] Sara: one more security thing — SSO and RBAC integration, SAML/Okta?
[05:48] Alex: yes, SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning, plus fine-grained RBAC in the console.
[05:54] Ethan: success criteria for the POC?
[05:57] Alex: agreed criteria: stable integration with LangChain, <150ms p50 for the chosen model on sandbox at expected prompt sizes, correct token accounting per-product-line, and a security sign-off on network/KMS.
[06:08] Maya: timeline: we want to decide within 3 weeks and run a 2-week POC.
[06:12] Alex: that works. we'll get you sandbox keys and security docs asap.
[06:16] Priya: i'll drop a starter repo with langchain and llamaindex examples, plus envoy config and prometheus alerts.
[06:22] Jon: on the envoy config, can you include an example for JWT auth + rate limiting by customer id?
[06:27] Priya: yes, we have that.
[06:29] Jon: cool. are there any known issues with long-running streamed responses behind an HTTP proxy? we saw timeouts in other setups.
[06:34] Priya: keep-alive and proxy buffering are key. in our docs we call out disable buffering, increase timeouts, and stream chunked responses. our sidecar also has logic to do chunked forwarding to avoid proxy buffering.
[06:47] Sara: can Redwood redact PCI-sensitive fields automatically in logs?
[06:51] Priya: yes, you can enable automatic PII/PCI redaction with custom regex rules; for private we can run that inline so data never lands unredacted in logs.
[07:01] Alex: ok let's recap next steps — Alex create sandbox, Priya send SOC2 and starter repo, Jon share gateway config.
[07:08] Maya: thanks, we look forward to the POC.
[07:10] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
